chapters.1.lds: The 2026 lesson connects faithful choices with resisting harmful pressures. How does the steward’s risk shape Daniel’s proposed trial?
chapters.1.summary: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon takes Jerusalem and carries off some temple vessels. He orders young men of noble families trained for his court. Daniel and three friends are chosen and given Babylonian names. They are to eat the king’s food and drink his wine. Daniel resolves not to defile himself and asks to be excused. The official fears for his own head. Daniel proposes ten days on vegetables and water. The four look healthier, and God gives them learning and wisdom.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson identifies the Church with the kingdom represented by the stone. This is a later Church application of the vision. Why does Daniel pray with his companions before answering?
chapters.2.summary: The king has a troubling dream and demands that his wise men tell it. They say no one can do this except the gods. He orders all the wise men killed. Daniel asks for time and prays with his friends. God reveals the dream in the night. The king saw a statue of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay. A stone cut without hands struck its feet and became a great mountain. Daniel says God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson studies faith that continues even when rescue is uncertain. What makes their refusal independent of rescue?
chapters.3.summary: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a huge gold image on a plain. All officials must bow when the music plays, or be thrown into a furnace. Three Jewish officials refuse. The king rages and asks what god can rescue them. They answer that their God is able to save them. Even if he does not, they will not worship the image. They are thrown in, and the king sees four men walking unharmed. He calls them out and praises their God.
chapters.4.lds: How does care for poor people relate to royal power?
chapters.4.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar tells this story himself in a letter to all peoples. He dreamed of a great tree that fed and sheltered every creature. A heavenly watcher ordered it cut down, with its stump left in the ground. Daniel explains that the tree is the king. He will live like an animal until he knows that heaven rules. Daniel urges him to do right and show mercy to the poor. A year later the king boasts about Babylon and loses his mind. When he looks up to heaven, his reason returns.
chapters.5.lds: Why does Daniel reject the rewards before explaining the writing?
chapters.5.summary: King Belshazzar gives a feast for a thousand nobles. He orders the gold cups from Jerusalem’s temple brought for his guests. They drink and praise gods of gold, silver, wood, and stone. A hand appears and writes on the wall. The king turns pale, and his wise men cannot read it. Daniel is called and refuses the king’s gifts. He reads the words: numbered, weighed, divided. That night Belshazzar is killed.
chapters.6.lds: The lesson connects Daniel’s regular prayer with daily faith. How does the prayer ban expose the king’s limits?
chapters.6.summary: King Darius appoints officials over the kingdom, and Daniel excels among them. His rivals can find no fault in his work. They persuade the king to ban prayer to anyone but himself for thirty days. Daniel goes home and prays three times a day, as before. The king is distressed and cannot undo his own law. Daniel is thrown to the lions, and the king spends a sleepless night. At dawn Daniel answers that God shut the lions’ mouths. The king orders respect for Daniel’s God.
chapters.7.lds: The lesson reads the humanlike figure through Jesus Christ. This Christian reading remains separate from the vision’s shared kingdom for the saints. Doctrine and Covenants 116 places the Ancient of Days at Adam-ondi-Ahman. Why does the explanation give the kingdom to the saints?
chapters.7.summary: Daniel dreams of four great beasts rising from a stormy sea. One is like a lion, one like a bear, and one like a leopard. The fourth is terrible, with iron teeth and ten horns. Thrones are set, and the Ancient of Days takes his seat. The court sits, and the books are opened. One like a son of man comes with the clouds and receives a lasting kingdom. An angel explains that the beasts are kingdoms. The holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom.
chapters.8.lds: What remains difficult after the animals receive named explanations?
chapters.8.summary: Daniel sees a ram with two horns pushing in every direction. A goat comes from the west and breaks the ram. The goat’s great horn is broken, and four grow in its place. A small horn grows and attacks the holy place and its daily offering. A voice asks how long this will last. Gabriel explains that the ram is Media and Persia and the goat is Greece. A fierce king will rise and be broken without human hand. Daniel is sick for days and does not understand.
chapters.9.lds: Why does Daniel appeal to mercy rather than earned reward?
chapters.9.summary: Daniel reads in Jeremiah that Jerusalem’s ruin would last seventy years. He turns to God with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes. He confesses that all Israel has sinned and ignored the prophets. God is in the right, and shame belongs to the people. He asks God to turn his anger from Jerusalem. He asks on the ground of mercy and for God’s own name. Gabriel comes while he is still praying. He speaks of seventy weeks set for the people and the holy city.
chapters.10.lds: How does the messenger help Daniel’s weakened body?
chapters.10.summary: In the third year of Cyrus, Daniel mourns for three weeks. Beside the Tigris he sees a man clothed in linen with a face like lightning. His companions run, and Daniel falls weak to the ground. A hand lifts him to his knees. The messenger says Daniel’s words were heard from the first day. The prince of Persia opposed him for twenty-one days until Michael came. Daniel cannot speak or breathe. The messenger touches him again and says, “Peace be to you.”
chapters.11.lds: Why does faithful teaching remain important when teachers suffer?
chapters.11.summary: The messenger describes a long line of kings. A mighty king rises, and his kingdom is divided to the four winds. Kings of the south and north make war and marriage alliances that fail. A hateful ruler gains power by flattery. He attacks the holy covenant and stops the daily offering. Those who know their God stand firm and act. The wise teach many, though some fall by sword and flame. The proud king exalts himself and comes to his end with no one to help.
chapters.12.lds: What does Daniel receive when full understanding remains unavailable?
chapters.12.summary: The messenger says a time of great trouble is coming. Daniel’s people will be rescued, all whose names are written in the book. Many who sleep in the dust will awake. Some rise to lasting life, and some to shame. The wise will shine like the sky. Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end. He hears and does not understand, and he asks about the outcome. He is told to go his way, rest, and rise at the end.
